defects: The conclusion DenseRange (fun x : F => fun i => x) is stated using a single arbitrary [TopologicalSpace F] instance applied uniformly to every coordinate of the product, rather than each coordinate carrying the distinct topology induced by v i (as the gold does via WithAbs (v i)). This completely disconnects the topological claim from the absolute values v, changing the meaning of the theorem (it no longer expresses that density holds w.r.t. the topologies induced by the v_i).

hv_nontrivial (∀ i, ∃ x, v i x ≠ 0) does not correctly formalize 'v i is a nontrivial absolute value'; since any valid AbsoluteValue satisfies v(1) = 1 ≠ 0, this hypothesis is vacuously true and adds no real constraint, unlike gold's (v i).IsNontrivial (which excludes the trivial/discrete absolute value).

hv_inequiv (∀ i j, i ≠ j → v i ≠ v j) formalizes pairwise distinctness of the absolute values as functions, not pairwise topological inequivalence (¬ IsEquiv) as in gold; two distinct but equivalent absolute values (e.g. v and a power of v) would satisfy this hypothesis while violating the mathematically required condition, making it strictly weaker/incorrect.
Uses [Fintype ι] instead of [Finite ι], a minor unnecessary strengthening of the finiteness hypothesis (data vs. Prop).
